comment: Take Dr. Charity for 150 if you can.  Asking questions during the labs certainly helps. You don't need to know an ounce of Python code before 150 to get an A. They do go a bit fast, but the lectures are all concise and well-structured. Make sure you review the lecture slides before each pop-quiz and you'll be good.

Dr. Charity is ideal for experienced coders who already understand the material. I would not recommend the class if you are a beginner coder. They are explaining the lecture really quickly, making it difficult to stay up. They have a pop quiz, however it is only implied

Dr. Charity is very kind accessible and helpful to beginner coders. They always re-explain and review things before exams and have practice problems available. The only point of difficulty is that they talk very fast which can make it take a little more effort to keep up as a beginner coder.

M is awesome!! If you're a beginner coder take them! They are hilarious and have an awesome energy. M made learning Python a lot of fun and made it very digestible with fun examples. There are ‘pop quizzes' but they're always hinted at. 100% would get a beer with them. :-)

I had never taken any kind of coding class before, but Dr. Charity explains things very well during lectures, which are Google Slides that they go through. There is a weekly lab which can usually be finished during the designated time. I highly recommend this professor. Great!

Dr. Charity was an amazing professor. They made complex computer science digestible for beginners. The lectures were amazing and they offered so many practice problems to go along, make sure you do them because they are exactly like the tests/quizzes. There are pop quizzes but they always hint at when they are going to happen so you can study.
